_comment: The adversarial instrument registry. `instrument.name` in an adversarial history entry is a foreign key INTO this file (ADR-027 rule 4), and until it existed the field was a foreign key to nothing: `--instrument-name does-not-exist` recorded happily, which is a row fingerprinting an object nobody can look up. The judge's half of the same idea is `quality/judge/frozen.json`.
_what_a_name_identifies: The CODE THAT READ THE RUN, and only that. A name resolves to the six computed digests below; two entries naming `m04-A` are comparable exactly because those six were identical both times. `guardrail_version` and `guardrail_policy_sha256` are deliberately NOT here: they describe what PRODUCED the observations, not what scored them, and a later run under a new guardrail version is still scored by this instrument. They stay in the entry, where they vary per run as they should.
_how_to_add_one: Never edit a registered instrument's digests. If the scorer, the semantics, the probe corpus, the G4 corpus, `classify.py` or the capture path moves, that is a DIFFERENT instrument: register a new name beside this one and leave the old row standing, so every published number keeps a resolvable description of what read it. Editing digests in place would silently redefine every entry that cites the name -- the exact substitution ADR-018 exists to prevent. ADR-038: the registration is a PRECONDITION for any scorer change, not a successor to it -- moving `scorer_sha256` makes the previously-registered row stop describing the tree, and the contract test is scoped so that only the MOST RECENTLY registered instrument must match it. Older rows are historical and exempt; that exemption is scoped to old rows and is NOT a subset check, which would let a future digest be dropped from a registered row unnoticed.

m04-A.why: The first adversarial instrument recorded under a name. It scores at k=3 with unanimity deciding (ADR-031), reads each probe's declared `pass_when`, and requires an audit record that resolves -- `resolve_failed` scores FAIL rather than reading as an ordinary miss.

m04-B.why: ADR-038. A guardrail block whose attribution names no control no longer satisfies the broad semantics -- the fail-closed reading `_satisfied_by` already argued for the narrow one, applied to the branch nine of the ten probes declare. An observation with NO `assessed` key predates the field and still passes, marked unearned. `semantics_sha256` now covers `_satisfied_by`'s source, because implementing a change to what a probe passing IS left the old digest byte-identical. Three G4 cases were added, including the positive control. NOTHING IS RE-SCORED UNDER THIS NAME HERE: the first entry citing it is produced by whatever run records one next.

m04-C.why: ADR-038 amendment 1. THREE defects, each of which made ADR-038's closure of the unattributed block untrue in practice. (1) `observation_from_record` now carries `assessed`, keyed on PRESENCE -- the probe harness copied it behind `if assessed:` and an empty list is falsy, so the one shape the rule exists to catch was the one shape routed around it: 9/10 PASS, marked unearned, which reads as honesty about a hole still being fallen into. (2) `score_samples` now propagates `unearned`; it built a fresh PASS and dropped the mark, so the honesty mark did not exist at k>1, which is M04's k and every future run's. (3) A guardrail block carrying NO attribution object at all is no longer read as the legacy population. An observation recorded under m04-B cannot be compared to one recorded here: the two disagree about whether an unattributed block is visible at all.

m04-D.why: ADR-040. A record says WHICH SIDE fired (`channels`, emitted on every intervention including empty), a probe declares the channels its payload travels on, and a block attributed only to channels the probe never reached no longer credits it -- shape B, measured 9/10 before and 0/10 after. Subset, never intersection. Observations with no `channels` key predate the field and are out of scope, a population that is closed because every intervention now emits the key and `test_contracts.py` pins it. `build_record`'s consistency check is symmetric in both directions with a test that it FIRES. A SEVENTH digest, `guardrail_sha256`, covers `core/guardrail.py` and `core/toolloop.py` -- the derivation and the assignment the verdict now turns on, which were in no digest and on no two-key path.
m04-D._registered_corrected: Recorded as 2026-08-23 when ADR-040 registered it; the commit is 2026-08-22 12:03:31 -0700 (bd0e247). Corrected by ADR-041, and NOT a cosmetic fix: the contract test resolves `the current instrument` by `registered` date, so a row dated in the future makes an OLDER instrument resolve as current and silently exempts the real one from having to describe this tree. Only the date moved -- no digest, no `why`, and no history entry cites this name.

m04-E.first_entry: none yet — registered as a PRECONDITION for the scorer change, not a successor to it. No suite is re-scored under it in this change; the first entry naming it is produced by whatever run records one next.
m04-E.why: ADR-041. Adds OUT_OF_SCOPE: a probe an arm's recorded run never ASKED is no longer INFRA. The L5 lane re-scores committed observations and does not run probes, so an eleventh probe had no historical observation on any arm and all three went INFRA at once -- exit 2, on every service's every PR, with a remediation naming an input nobody can fix. m00b had no gateway and m01 ran under an undeployed guardrail, so neither can ever supply one; without this the corpus was frozen at ten probes. Scope is read from the arm's own `_asked` manifest, never declared by the probe: a deletion then contradicts the record instead of making a declaration true. `semantics_sha256` gains `_scope_verdict` and `asked_from`, because whether a probe is scored on an arm IS what its result means -- measured byte-identical without them. Observations recorded under m04-D and under this instrument disagree about whether an unasked probe is visible at all, which is what a separate instrument name is for.
